gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's Nano Charging Station 67W (A9129), the pick it labels 'Fast charging … up to 67W', does not support Samsung's 45W Super Fast Charging 2.0. Anker supports Super Fast Charging only on the S21, S22 and S23 Ultra. With all four USB ports in use, its two USB-C ports drop to 20 W and 30 W, and USB-C2 takes priority over USB-C1.
standout_why: Compared against rottenwifi.com, itechguides.com, laptopbee.com, geekchamp.com and anker.com/blogs/hubs-and-docks/best-power-strip. All five pages say nothing about Samsung Super Fast Charging, 45W or PPS. None gives the A9129 per-combination split or its port-priority rule. Rottenwifi and laptopbee already state that the Anker 351's USB-C reaches 20 W only when the USB-A ports are idle, so that point is not new. The Anker blog already gives the A9128's 1,000 W AC limit. None of these pages says the A9128 has no surge protection, which Anker states on its product page. Tom's Guide, the only cited rival, returned no body text through WebFetch, so I could not check it directly.
decides: This confirms the Anker 351 (A9192) as the general pick for phones and earbuds. It also qualifies the A9129: it is a 67 W single-port charger, and a Galaxy S24/S25-class phone cannot use its 45 W mode on it. For a laptop plus phone charging together, the A9128 (65 W + 60 W with three ports) is the better fit. But Anker says the A9128 has no surge protection and limits AC to 1,000 W (10 A). It also needs a 5A e-marker cable for anything above 60 W. So it should not be someone's only protection for a desk full of equipment.
